question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A form of government in which power is held by the wealthy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Plutocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Plutocracy" means government by the wealthy, from the Greek “ploutos” (wealth) and “kratos” (power, rule). (धनाढ्यों द्वारा शासित सरकार)
◦ Example: Critics argue that unchecked corporate influence is turning the democracy into a plutocracy.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes a system or form of government or rule, and the first part of the word tells us who or what holds the power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Aristocracy (अभिजात वर्ग का शासन): Government by a small privileged class, especially a hereditary nobility.

 

• Option 3: Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government by religious leaders claiming divine sanction, from Greek “theos” (god).

 

• Option 4: Meritocracy (योग्यता-तंत्र): Government or leadership by people selected on the basis of their ability or merit.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy/-crat" words frequently asked in SSC: Aristocracy (rule by the nobility), Theocracy (rule by religious authority), Meritocracy (rule by the most able), Bureaucracy (rule by officials), Autocracy (rule by one person with absolute power), Democracy (rule by the people) and Kleptocracy (rule by thieves).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person who loves luxury

2. Bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी): A person who loves or collects books

3. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others to gain advantage

4. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान दक्षता से काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

5. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person with no fixed home who moves from place to place

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who hates or distrusts mankind in general.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Misanthrope.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Misanthrope" means one who hates or distrusts mankind, from the Greek “misein” (to hate) and “anthropos” (man, mankind). (मानव-जाति से घृणा करने वाला)
◦ Example: After being betrayed repeatedly, he became a bitter misanthrope who avoided all company.

 

• The root "anthropos" (mankind) appears in several SSC-relevant words such as “philanthropist” (lover of mankind) and “anthropology” (study of mankind), while the prefix "mis-" denotes hatred or hostility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Philanthropist (परोपकारी): One who works for the welfare of others and loves mankind, from Greek “philein” (to love) and “anthropos” (mankind).

 

• Option 3: Xenophobe (विदेशियों से घृणा करने वाला): A person who fears or hates foreigners or strangers, from Greek “xenos” (stranger).

 

• Option 4: Cynic (निंदक): A person who believes people are motivated purely by self-interest and distrusts human sincerity.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Misanthrope" frequently asked in SSC: Philanthropist (one who loves and helps mankind), Xenophobe (one who hates foreigners), Egoist (one concerned only with oneself), Cynic (one who distrusts human motives) and Recluse (one who lives in seclusion, avoiding others).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Hermit (सन्यासी): A person who lives in solitude, often for religious reasons

2. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders from place to place without a home

3. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

4. Numismatist (मुद्राशास्त्री/सिक्का संग्रहकर्ता): A person who studies or collects coins

5. Bibliomaniac (पुस्तकों के प्रति उन्मत्त प्रेम रखने वाला): A person with an excessive love of collecting books

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A dramatic or literary style marked by exaggerated emotions, sensational events, and stereotyped characters.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Melodrama.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Melodrama" means a sensational dramatic piece marked by exaggerated characters and appeals to the emotions, from the Greek “melos” (song, music) and “drama” (action, play). (अतिशय भावुक लेखन शैली)
◦ Example: The film was criticized as a melodrama full of exaggerated emotions and improbable coincidences.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Satire (व्यंग्य): A literary style that uses irony, ridicule, or wit to criticize vice or folly.

 

• Option 2: Tragedy (त्रासदी): A serious dramatic work in which the main character suffers a disastrous fate, often ending in death.

 

• Option 4: Farce (प्रहसन): A comic dramatic work relying on improbable situations, exaggerated characters, and slapstick for humour.

 

NOTE

 

• Other literary/dramatic style words close in meaning to "Melodrama" frequently asked in SSC: Satire (ridicules vice through wit), Tragedy (a serious play with an unhappy ending), Comedy (a light, humorous play with a happy ending), Farce (broad comedy of improbable situations), Burlesque (a mocking imitation) and Parody (a comic imitation of a work).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Egoist (स्वार्थी/अहंवादी): A person who thinks only of themselves

2. Altruist (परोपकारी): A person unselfishly concerned for others' welfare

3. Optimist (आशावादी): A person who has a hopeful view of things

4. Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who expects the worst outcome

5. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी): A shy, reserved person absorbed in their own thoughts

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

To harass or urge someone persistently and annoyingly with requests or demands.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Importune.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Importune" means to harass or urge someone with persistent, repeated requests, from the Latin “importunus” (unsuitable, troublesome). (बार-बार तंग करना)
◦ Example: Beggars would importune passers-by for money outside the temple.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Beseech (विनती करना): To ask someone earnestly or urgently for something, often out of desperation.

 

• Option 2: Cajole (फुसलाना): To persuade someone to do something by sustained flattery or coaxing.

 

• Option 3: Solicit (याचना करना): To ask for or try to obtain something from someone, often formally.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Importune" frequently asked in SSC: Beseech (to beg earnestly), Solicit (to ask for formally), Cajole (to coax with flattery), Entreat (to ask earnestly) and Supplicate (to beg humbly).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी): An outgoing, sociable person

2. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion, avoiding others

3. Fastidious (छिद्रान्वेषी/चूजी): Very attentive to detail and hard to please

4. Iconoclast (परंपरा भंजक): A person who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions

5. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A fanatical and uncompromising supporter of a cause

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The school, college, or university that a person previously attended.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Alma Mater.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Alma Mater" means the school, college, or university that one previously attended, from the Latin “alma” (nourishing) and “mater” (mother) — literally "nourishing mother." (जहाँ पढ़ाई की हो वह विद्यालय/कॉलेज)
◦ Example: She returned to her alma mater to deliver the convocation address.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Alumnus (पूर्व छात्र): A former student or graduate of a particular school, college, or university.

 

• Option 3: Curriculum (पाठ्यक्रम): The subjects or courses that make up a programme of study at a school or college.

 

• Option 4: Sabbatical (अध्ययन-अवकाश): A period of paid leave granted to a teacher or academic for study or travel.

 

NOTE

 

• Other education-related words close in meaning to "Alma Mater" frequently asked in SSC: Alumnus/Alumna (a former student), Curriculum (course of study), Sabbatical (a period of leave for study), Campus (grounds of a college) and Dean (an academic administrative head).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारों वाला व्यक्ति): An unorthodox, independent-minded person

2. Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभाशाली बालक): A young person with exceptional talent

3. Virtuoso (कुशल कलाकार): A person highly skilled in an art, especially music

4. Charlatan (ढोंगी): A person falsely claiming to have expert knowledge or skill

5. Impostor (प्रतिरूपक/धोखेबाज़): A person who pretends to be someone else

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes in or worships more than one god.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Polytheist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Polytheist" means a believer in or worshipper of many gods, from the Greek “polys” (many) and “theos” (god). (अनेक देवताओं में विश्वास करने वाला)
◦ Example: Ancient Greek and Roman religions were polytheist in nature, worshipping numerous deities.

 

• The suffix "-theist" always relates to belief in god(s), and the prefix attached tells us the nature of that belief (mono- one, poly- many, a- none, pan- all).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Monotheist (एकेश्वरवादी): A person who believes in the existence of only one god.

 

• Option 3: Atheist (नास्तिक): A person who does not believe in the existence of any god.

 

• Option 4: Pantheist (सर्वेश्वरवादी): A person who believes that God and the universe are identical.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-theist" words frequently asked in SSC: Monotheist (believes in one god), Atheist (believes in no god), Pantheist (believes God is present in everything), Agnostic (believes the existence of God cannot be known) and Deist (believes in a creator God who does not intervene in the world).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Renegade (धर्मत्यागी/विद्रोही): A person who deserts and betrays an organization or cause

2. Turncoat (पाला बदलने वाला): A person who changes their loyalty or principles

3. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A soldier who fights for payment rather than for a cause

4. Vegan (शुद्ध शाकाहारी): A person who eats no animal products

5. Carnivore (मांसाहारी): An animal or person that eats meat

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An imagined perfect society or place, free from suffering, poverty, and injustice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Utopia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Utopia" means an imagined ideal society or place where everything is perfect and free from suffering, from the Greek “ou” (not) and “topos” (place) — literally "no place," coined by Sir Thomas More. (आदर्श दुःख-रहित समाज)
◦ Example: The novel describes a utopia where poverty, crime, and disease do not exist.

 

• The suffix "-topia" relates to an imagined place or society; its opposite, "dystopia" (from Greek “dys-”, bad), describes a frightening, oppressive imagined society.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Dystopia (दुखद काल्पनिक समाज): An imagined society or place that is dehumanizing, oppressive, or undesirable — the opposite of a utopia.

 

• Option 2: Anarchy (अराजकता): A state of society with no government or law and order, resulting in disorder.

 

• Option 4: Oligarchy (अल्पतंत्र): A form of government in which power rests with a small group of people.

 

NOTE

 

• Other society/government-related words close in meaning to "Utopia" frequently asked in SSC: Dystopia (a nightmarish imagined society), Anarchy (absence of government), Oligarchy (rule by a few), Elysium (a place of perfect happiness) and Arcadia (an idyllic, peaceful rural paradise).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Herbivore (शाकाहारी प्राणी): An animal that eats only plants

2. Omnivore (सर्वाहारी): An animal or person that eats both plants and meat

3. Insomniac (अनिद्रा-रोगी): A person who habitually finds it hard to sleep

4. Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला): A person who walks about while asleep

5. Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An abnormal fear of confined spaces

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who completely abstains from drinking alcohol.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Teetotaler.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Teetotaler" means a person who completely abstains from drinking alcohol, believed to derive from an emphatic reduplication of "total" (as in "T-total") used in 19th-century temperance pledges. (जो बिल्कुल शराब नहीं पीता)
◦ Example: Being a strict teetotaler, he ordered only a soft drink at the party.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Glutton (पेटू): A person who eats or drinks excessively.

 

• Option 2: Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practises strict self-denial and avoids all forms of physical indulgence.

 

• Option 3: Vegetarian (शाकाहारी): A person who does not eat meat or fish.

 

NOTE

 

• Other lifestyle/habit-related words close in meaning to "Teetotaler" frequently asked in SSC: Ascetic (practises strict self-denial), Vegan (eats no animal products), Vegetarian (eats no meat), Glutton (eats/drinks excessively) and Epicure (one with refined taste in food and drink).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Acrophobia (ऊँचाई का भय): An abnormal fear of heights

2. Agoraphobia (खुले/भीड़भाड़ वाले स्थानों का भय): An abnormal fear of open or crowded spaces

3. Hydrophobia (जल का भय): An abnormal fear of water

4. Xenophile (विदेशी लोगों/संस्कृति का प्रेमी): A person attracted to foreign peoples or cultures

5. Anglophile (अंग्रेजी संस्कृति का प्रशंसक): A person who greatly admires England or English culture

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An expert who studies the composition, structure, and physical properties of minerals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mineralogist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Mineralogist" means an expert who studies the composition, structure, and properties of minerals, from the Latin “minera” (mine, ore) and the Greek suffix “-logia” (study of). (चट्टानों व खनिजों का विशेषज्ञ)
◦ Example: The mineralogist examined the rock sample to identify the minerals it contained.

 

• The suffix "-logist" always denotes a person who studies or is an expert in a particular subject, indicated by the first part of the word (e.g., mineral-, geo-, seismo-, entomo-).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Geologist (भूविज्ञानी): An expert who studies the physical structure, substance, and history of the Earth.

 

• Option 3: Seismologist (भूकंपविज्ञानी): A scientist who studies earthquakes and related phenomena.

 

• Option 4: Entomologist (कीटविज्ञानी): A scientist who studies insects.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-logist" words frequently asked in SSC: Geologist (studies the Earth's structure), Seismologist (studies earthquakes), Entomologist (studies insects), Ornithologist (studies birds), Petrologist (studies rocks) and Herpetologist (studies reptiles and amphibians).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Technophobe (तकनीक से डरने वाला): A person who fears or dislikes new technology

2. Astronaut (अंतरिक्ष यात्री): A person trained to travel in a spacecraft

3. Aeronaut (वैमानिक): A traveller in a balloon or airship

4. Bureaucrat (नौकरशाह): An official in a government department

5. Autocrat (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler who has absolute power

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who takes great pleasure in eating, often consuming large quantities of food.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Gourmand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Gourmand" means a person who takes great enthusiasm and pleasure in eating, often in large quantities, from the Old French “gourmant.” (खाने-पीने का बहुत शौकीन)
◦ Example: As a self-confessed gourmand, he could never resist a second helping at dinner.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Epicure (भोजन का पारखी): A person with refined and discriminating taste in food and drink, valuing quality over quantity.

 

• Option 3: Glutton (पेटू): A person who eats and drinks excessively, especially to the point of greed.

 

• Option 4: Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of taste, particularly in art, food, or wine.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Gourmand" frequently asked in SSC: Epicure (a person of refined taste in food), Gourmet (a connoisseur of good food and drink), Glutton (one who eats excessively), Connoisseur (an expert judge of taste) and Bon vivant (one who lives luxuriously and enjoys good food).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Demagogue (लोकरंजक नेता): A political leader who appeals to popular passions and prejudices

2. Diplomat (राजनयिक): An official who represents a country in dealings with other nations

3. Ambassador (राजदूत): A diplomatic representative of a country stationed abroad

4. Litterateur (साहित्यकार): A person devoted to literature or literary studies

5. Polyglot (बहुभाषाविद्): A person who knows and can speak several languages

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who favours traditional values and institutions and is resistant to change.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Conservative.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Conservative" means a person who favours the preservation of existing traditions and institutions and resists change, from the Latin “conservare” (to preserve). (पुरानी व्यवस्था का समर्थक)
◦ Example: As a conservative, he opposed the sweeping reforms proposed by the new government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Radical (चरमपंथी): A person who advocates thorough or extreme political and social reform.

 

• Option 2: Liberal (उदारवादी): A person open to new ideas and favouring reform, individual freedom, and gradual change.

 

• Option 4: Progressive (प्रगतिशील): A person who favours new ideas, social change, and reform, often moving away from tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Other political-ideology words close in meaning to "Conservative" frequently asked in SSC: Radical (favours extreme reform), Liberal (favours reform and freedom), Progressive (favours change and modernization), Reactionary (seeks to return to a former state of affairs) and Moderate (holds balanced, non-extreme views).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Linguist (भाषाविद्): A person skilled in languages or the study of linguistics

2. Orator (वाक्पटु वक्ता): A skilled and eloquent public speaker

3. Elocutionist (भाषण-कला में निपुण व्यक्ति): A person skilled in the art of clear and expressive public speaking

4. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): One who copies another's work and passes it off as their own

5. Forger (जालसाज़): A person who makes fraudulent copies or imitations of something

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A sentimental longing or wistful affection for a period in the past.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nostalgia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Nostalgia" means a sentimental longing or wistful affection for a period in the past, from the Greek “nostos” (return home) and “algos” (pain). (अतीत की याद में भावुक होना)
◦ Example: Looking through the old photographs filled her with nostalgia for her school days.

 

• The suffix "-algia" relates to pain or a longing, distressing feeling, seen also in words like "neuralgia" (nerve pain) and "myalgia" (muscle pain).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reverie (दिवास्वप्न): A state of being pleasantly absorbed in one's own thoughts, a daydream.

 

• Option 2: Melancholy (उदासी): A deep, persistent feeling of sadness or gloom, without a specific cause.

 

• Option 3: Wanderlust (घूमने की तीव्र इच्छा): A strong innate desire to travel and explore the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Nostalgia" frequently asked in SSC: Reverie (a daydream), Melancholy (persistent sadness), Wanderlust (desire to travel), Reminiscence (the act of recalling past experiences) and Homesickness (longing for one's home).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Smuggler (तस्कर): A person who moves goods illegally into or out of a country

2. Poacher (अवैध शिकारी): A person who hunts or fishes illegally

3. Vandal (विध्वंसक): A person who deliberately destroys or damages property

4. Anarchist (अराजकतावादी): A person who believes in the abolition of all government

5. Patriot (देशभक्त): A person who loves and loyally supports their country

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is learning a trade or craft under the supervision of a skilled worker.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Apprentice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Apprentice" means a person learning a trade or craft under the guidance of a skilled worker, typically under a formal agreement, from the Latin “apprehendere” (to grasp, to learn). (प्रशिक्षु/शिष्य)
◦ Example: He worked as an apprentice to a master carpenter for five years before setting up his own workshop.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Novice (नौसिखिया): A person who is new to and inexperienced in a particular field or activity.

 

• Option 3: Mentor (मार्गदर्शक): An experienced and trusted advisor who guides someone less experienced.

 

• Option 4: Veteran (अनुभवी व्यक्ति): A person who has had long experience in a particular field.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Apprentice" frequently asked in SSC: Novice (a beginner, new to a field), Trainee (a person being trained for a job), Neophyte (a person new to a subject or activity), Tyro (a beginner or novice) and Protégé (a person guided and supported by an experienced mentor).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Traitor (देशद्रोही): A person who betrays their country, cause, or friend

2. Martyr (शहीद): A person who suffers or dies for the sake of a cause

3. Ambivert (उभयमुखी व्यक्ति): A person having a balance of introvert and extrovert traits

4. Pedant (पंडिताऊ व्यक्ति): A person overly concerned with minor details or formal rules

5. Nihilist (शून्यवादी): A person who rejects all religious and moral principles

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

One who lives in solitude, deliberately avoiding the company of others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Recluse.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Recluse" means a person who lives in solitude, deliberately avoiding the company of others. (एकांत में रहने वाला)
◦ Example: After his wife's death, he became a recluse and rarely left his house.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Hermit (संन्यासी): A person who lives in solitude, especially for religious reasons.

 

• Option 3: Vagrant (आवारा): A person without a settled home who wanders from place to place.

 

• Option 4: Misanthrope (मनुष्य-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes and avoids other people, from the Greek “misos” (hatred) and “anthropos” (man).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Recluse" frequently asked in SSC: Hermit (lives in seclusion, often for religious reasons), Anchorite (a religious recluse), Ascetic (practises severe self-discipline), Misanthrope (hates mankind), Vagrant (a wandering homeless person) and Solitary (a person who prefers to be alone).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who works for others' welfare

2. Bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी): A person who loves and collects books

3. Cynic (निंदक/संशयवादी): A person who distrusts others' motives

4. Nomad (घुमंतू): A person with no permanent home who wanders

5. Optimist (आशावादी): A person who expects the best outcome

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Self-punishment or deep sorrow felt for having committed a sin or wrongdoing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Penitence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Penitence" means deep or genuine sorrow and self-reproach for having done wrong, especially a sin, from the Latin “paenitere” (to repent, to regret). (पाप के लिए पश्चाताप)
◦ Example: The prisoner showed genuine penitence for his crimes.

 

• Words from the Latin root "paenitere" (to repent) include penitent, penance, and repentant, all relating to remorse for wrongdoing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Repugnance (घृणा): A strong feeling of dislike or disgust.

 

• Option 2: Reticence (मौन): The quality of being reserved or reluctant to speak about one's thoughts.

 

• Option 4: Persistence (दृढ़ता): Firm and continued action despite difficulty or opposition.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Penitence" frequently asked in SSC: Repentance (regret for one's wrongdoing), Contrition (deep remorse for sin), Remorse (guilt felt after wrongdoing), Penance (self-imposed punishment as atonement), Atonement (reparation for a wrong) and Compunction (a feeling of guilt).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Aphorism (सूक्ति): A short, pithy statement of a general truth

2. Gourmet (स्वादिष्ट भोजन का पारखी): A connoisseur of good food

3. Truant (स्कूल से जानबूझकर अनुपस्थित रहने वाला): A student who stays away from school without permission

4. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person fanatically committed to a cause

5. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारों वाला व्यक्ति): An unorthodox or independent-minded person

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

One who believes that everything that happens is predetermined and therefore inevitable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fatalist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Fatalist" means a person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate and therefore inevitable, from the Latin “fatum” (that which is spoken; destiny). (भाग्यवाद में विश्वास करने वाला)
◦ Example: Being a fatalist, he never worried about the outcome, believing it was already decided.

 

• The suffix "-ist" denotes a person who believes in or practises a particular doctrine, and the first part of the word names that doctrine (here, "fatal-", from "fate").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Idealist (आदर्शवादी): A person guided by ideals who pursues perfection rather than practical considerations.

 

• Option 2: Pragmatist (व्यवहारवादी): A person who deals with things practically rather than theoretically.

 

• Option 3: Nihilist (शून्यवादी): A person who rejects all religious and moral principles, believing life is meaningless.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-ist" words frequently asked in SSC: Optimist (believes in the best outcome), Pessimist (believes in the worst outcome), Realist (sees things as they really are), Anarchist (believes in the abolition of government), Egoist (believes only in self-interest) and Altruist (believes in selfless concern for others).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान रूप से काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

2. Glutton (पेटू): A person who eats and drinks excessively

3. Prodigal (फिजूलखर्च): A person who spends money wastefully

4. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of art or taste

5. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others for self-interest

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Living, growing, or taking place in or near water.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Aquatic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aquatic" means living, growing, or taking place in or near water, from the Latin “aqua” (water). (जल में रहने वाला)
◦ Example: Dolphins and whales are well-known aquatic mammals.

 

• Habitat-related adjectives often carry distinct Latin roots: "aqua" (water) → aquatic, "terra" (land) → terrestrial, and "arbor" (tree) → arboreal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Terrestrial (स्थलीय): Living on or relating to land, from the Latin “terra” (earth).

 

• Option 3: Arboreal (वृक्षों पर रहने वाला): Living in or relating to trees, from the Latin “arbor” (tree).

 

• Option 4: Aerial (वायवीय): Living, existing, or taking place in the air.

 

NOTE

 

• Other habitat-related words frequently asked in SSC: Terrestrial (living on land), Arboreal (living in trees), Aerial (living in air), Amphibious (living both on land and in water), Subterranean (living underground) and Marine (belonging to the sea).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nocturnal (रात्रिचर): Active mainly at night

2. Herbivorous (शाकाहारी): An animal that feeds only on plants

3. Migratory (प्रवासी): Moving from one region to another seasonally

4. Carnivorous (मांसाहारी): An animal that feeds on flesh

5. Omnivorous (सर्वाहारी): An animal or person that eats both plants and animals

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is overly self-centered and has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Narcissist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Narcissist" means a person who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves, from the Greek mythological figure “Narcissus”, who fell in love with his own reflection. (खुद से ही प्रेम करनेवाला)
◦ Example: He was such a narcissist that he could talk about nothing but his own achievements.

 

• The suffix "-ist" denotes a person characterised by a particular belief, trait, or practice, as also seen in "egoist", "altruist", and "hedonist".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Egoist (स्वार्थी): A person who acts primarily out of self-interest.

 

• Option 3: Altruist (परमार्थी): A person who selflessly cares for the welfare of others.

 

• Option 4: Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is the highest good, from the Greek “hedone” (pleasure).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words describing personality traits frequently asked in SSC: Egoist (acts from self-interest), Altruist (selflessly helps others), Hedonist (pursues pleasure as the highest good), Egotist (talks about oneself excessively), Misanthrope (hates mankind) and Philanthropist (works for human welfare).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Chauvinist (कट्टर पक्षपाती): One who is excessively or blindly devoted to one's own group

2. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी): A person who is shy and reserved

3. Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी): A person who is outgoing and socially confident

4. Skeptic (संशयवादी): A person who doubts accepted beliefs

5. Stoic (सहनशील/धैर्यवान): A person who endures hardship without complaint

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Unable to pay one's debts as they fall due.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Insolvent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Insolvent" means unable to pay one's debts as they fall due, from the Latin “in-” (not) and “solvere” (to loosen, to pay). (दिवालिया)
◦ Example: The company was declared insolvent after failing to repay its loans.

 

• The prefix "in-" means not, turning "solvent" (able to pay one's debts) into its opposite, "insolvent" (unable to pay one's debts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Affluent (धनी/समृद्ध): Having a great deal of money or wealth.

 

• Option 2: Extravagant (फिजूलखर्च): Spending money without restraint; excessively wasteful.

 

• Option 4: Frugal (मितव्ययी): Careful and economical in the use of money or resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Insolvent" frequently asked in SSC: Bankrupt (legally declared unable to pay debts), Destitute (extremely poor, lacking basic necessities), Impecunious (having little or no money), Indigent (poor, needy) and Penniless (having no money at all).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): One who copies another's work and claims it as one's own

2. Vandal (बर्बरतापूर्वक संपत्ति नष्ट करने वाला): A person who deliberately destroys or damages property

3. Miser (कंजूस): A person who hoards money and hates spending it

4. Novice (नौसिखिया): A beginner or inexperienced person

5. Veteran (अनुभवी): A person with long experience in a particular field

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The art of beautiful and decorative handwriting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Calligraphy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Calligraphy" means the art of beautiful and decorative handwriting, from the Greek “kallos” (beauty) and “graphein” (to write). (सुंदर लेखन की कला)
◦ Example: The ancient manuscript was admired for its exquisite calligraphy.

 

• The suffix "-graphy" always denotes writing, recording, or a descriptive art or science, and the first part of the word tells us what is being written or recorded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Choreography (नृत्य-रचना कला): The art of designing and composing sequences of dance movement.

 

• Option 2: Cartography (मानचित्रकला): The art or practice of drawing maps.

 

• Option 3: Typography (मुद्रण-कला): The art or style of arranging and designing printed type.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-graphy" words frequently asked in SSC: Choreography (art of composing dance), Cartography (art of map-making), Typography (art of arranging printed type), Photography (art of capturing images with light), Biography (an account of someone's life) and Geography (study of the earth's physical features).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambiguous (अस्पष्ट/द्विअर्थी): Open to more than one interpretation

2. Anecdote (किस्सा): A short amusing or interesting story about a real incident

3. Eloquent (वाकपटु): Fluent and persuasive in speaking

4. Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण): Using more words than necessary

5. Taciturn (मितभाषी): Reserved and saying very little

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Graceful, self-assured, and well-balanced behavior or bearing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Poise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Poise" means graceful, self-assured, and well-balanced behaviour or bearing, from the Old French “pois” (weight), ultimately from the Latin “pendere” (to weigh, to hang). (संतुलित और सौम्य आचरण)
◦ Example: She handled the difficult interview questions with remarkable poise.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Decorum (शालीनता): Behaviour that is polite and respects social conventions.

 

• Option 3: Nonchalance (उदासीनता): A casual lack of concern or anxiety.

 

• Option 4: Arrogance (अहंकार): An offensive display of superiority or self-importance.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Poise" frequently asked in SSC: Decorum (correct or polite behaviour), Composure (calmness of manner), Aplomb (self-confident assurance), Equanimity (mental calmness in difficult situations), Nonchalance (casual indifference) and Grace (elegance of movement or manner).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Candid (स्पष्टवादी/निष्कपट): Truthful and straightforward

2. Meticulous (बारीकी से ध्यान देने वाला): Very careful and precise about details

3. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Fond of company; sociable

4. Frivolous (तुच्छ/छिछोरा): Not having any serious purpose; silly

5. Austere (कठोर/सादगीपूर्ण): Severely simple and plain in appearance

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is highly educated or skilled in a specific field.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Expert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Expert" means a person who has comprehensive and authoritative knowledge or skill in a particular field, from the Latin “expertus” (tried, tested, proved). (किसी क्षेत्र का विशेषज्ञ)
◦ Example: She consulted an expert before investing in the stock market.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Amateur (शौकिया): A person who engages in an activity as a pastime rather than a profession.

 

• Option 3: Layman (सामान्य व्यक्ति): A person without specialized or professional knowledge in a particular field.

 

• Option 4: Dilettante (सतही रुचि रखने वाला): A person with only a superficial interest in a subject.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Expert" frequently asked in SSC: Amateur (does something for pleasure, not as a profession), Layman (a person without specialist knowledge), Dilettante (a dabbler with superficial interest), Novice (a beginner), Virtuoso (highly skilled in an art, especially music) and Connoisseur (an expert judge of taste).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Virtuoso (कलाकुशल/निपुण कलाकार): A person highly skilled in an art, especially music

2. Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभा वाला बालक): A young person with exceptional talent

3. Charlatan (ढोंगी/धोखेबाज): A person falsely claiming to have expert knowledge

4. Quack (नीम-हकीम/झोलाछाप): A person who falsely claims to have medical skill

5. Impostor (पाखंडी/धोखेबाज़ व्यक्ति): A person who pretends to be someone else

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A medicine or drug that has a calming or soothing effect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sedative.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Sedative" means a medicine or drug that induces calmness or sleep by reducing nervous excitement, from the Latin “sedare” (to calm, to settle). (शांत करनेवाली दवा)
◦ Example: The doctor prescribed a mild sedative to help him sleep.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Stimulant (उत्तेजक औषधि): A substance that increases physiological or nervous activity.

 

• Option 2: Antidote (विषनाशक औषधि): A medicine that counteracts a particular poison.

 

• Option 4: Analgesic (पीड़ानाशक औषधि): A medicine that relieves pain.

 

NOTE

 

• Other medicine-related words frequently asked in SSC: Stimulant (increases physiological activity), Antidote (counteracts a poison), Analgesic (relieves pain), Antiseptic (prevents infection by inhibiting growth of microorganisms), Antibiotic (destroys or inhibits bacteria) and Anaesthetic (causes loss of sensation or consciousness).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Antiseptic (पूतिरोधक): A substance that prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms

2. Antibiotic (प्रतिजैविक): A medicine that destroys or inhibits the growth of bacteria

3. Anaesthetic (बेहोशी की दवा): A substance that induces loss of sensation or consciousness

4. Placebo (मिथ्या औषधि): A substance with no therapeutic effect given to satisfy a patient

5. Panacea (रामबाण/सर्वरोगनाशक): A solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who studies the stars, outer space, and the physical universe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Astronomer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Astronomer" means a scientist who studies celestial objects, outer space, and the physical universe, from the Greek “astron” (star) and “nomos” (law, arrangement). (तारों और अंतरिक्ष का वैज्ञानिक)
◦ Example: The astronomer discovered a new exoplanet using a powerful telescope.

 

• The word "Astronomer" is frequently confused with "Astrologer" in SSC exams — an astronomer studies celestial science, while an astrologer studies the supposed influence of stars on human destiny.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Astrologer (ज्योतिषी): A person who studies the supposed influence of stars and planets on human affairs.

 

• Option 2: Meteorologist (मौसम वैज्ञानिक): A person who studies weather and climate.

 

• Option 3: Geologist (भूविज्ञानी): A person who studies the earth's physical structure and substances, especially rocks.

 

NOTE

 

• Other scientist/specialist words frequently asked in SSC: Astrologer (studies influence of stars on human affairs), Meteorologist (studies weather), Geologist (studies rocks and the earth's structure), Seismologist (studies earthquakes), Botanist (studies plants) and Zoologist (studies animals).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Seismologist (भूकंप वैज्ञानिक): A scientist who studies earthquakes

2. Botanist (वनस्पति वैज्ञानिक): A person who studies plant life

3. Zoologist (प्राणि वैज्ञानिक): A person who studies animals

4. Entomologist (कीट वैज्ञानिक): A person who studies insects

5. Ornithologist (पक्षी वैज्ञानिक): A person who studies birds

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who compiles or writes dictionaries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Lexicographer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Lexicographer" means a person who compiles or writes dictionaries, from the Greek “lexikon” (word-book) and “graphein” (to write). (शब्दकोश तैयार करनेवाला)
◦ Example: Samuel Johnson is remembered as one of the greatest English lexicographers.

 

• The suffix "-grapher" always denotes a person who writes, draws, or records something, and the first part of the word tells us what is written or recorded (here, "lexikon" = word-book).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Biographer (जीवनी लेखक): A person who writes an account of someone else's life.

 

• Option 3: Cartographer (मानचित्रकार): A person who draws or produces maps.

 

• Option 4: Stenographer (आशुलिपिक): A person skilled in shorthand writing.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-grapher" words frequently asked in SSC: Biographer (writes another's life story), Autobiographer (writes their own life story), Cartographer (draws maps), Stenographer (writes in shorthand), Choreographer (designs dance sequences) and Photographer (captures images with light).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Autobiographer (आत्मकथा लेखक): A person who writes the story of their own life

2. Numismatist (मुद्राशास्त्री): A person who collects or studies coins

3. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

4. Antiquarian (प्राचीन वस्तुओं का संग्रहकर्ता): A person who studies or collects antiques

5. Genealogist (वंशावली विशेषज्ञ): A person who studies family history and lineage
